name: smart_iceberg_margin_ratio_display
doc:
Row 7 — margin ratio (`mgnRatio`): `treatAsPercentage` (×100) then
`toLocalizedStringDownToFixed:2` — [`RoundingMode::Floor`], fixed 2
decimals, locale `%`.

Emitted as a [`BotDisplayText::Percent`], the SAME variant as row 5. The two
rows end in an identical native pair (`treatAsPercentage` +
`toLocalizedStringDownToFixed:2`), so they must render identically; only the
pre-processing differs (row 5 adds the clamp + per-sign truncation).

Canonical precedent for this exact native leaf:
`public::interactors::grid::contract_grid::detail::percent_down_fixed2_display`
— "renderer-side ×100 + DOWN + fixed 2 + `%`". That helper is private to the
contract-grid detail module and passes the raw value with
`pre_scaled: false`; here Rust applies the ×100 itself (`pre_scaled: true`)
to stay consistent with [`smart_iceberg_pnl_ratio_display`] next door, which
MUST scale in Rust because its truncation happens at the pre-×100 magnitude.

Native sets no `suffixText` on this row, so the cell's key label carries no
parenthesised unit — the `%` rides on the value, as it does natively.

Needs no instrument — pure arithmetic, so it can never go stale.

name: create
doc:
Create the pending-orders interactor.

`last_price` SEEDS the benefit-ratio (`% to fill`) baseline so the first
HTTP render already carries a real ticker, byte-identical to legacy
`GridPendingOrderPresenter` which primes `mapper.lastPrice` from
`requestBatchMarketTicker()` (the bot's market last price) BEFORE the
`tickers` WS subscription delivers a frame. Without it, the per-row
`benefit_ratio_display` was starved (`ticker_price == None`) until the
first WS push, so EVERY row's `% to fill` rendered the empty "" → "--".
The bot's `lastPrice` is the same value the native caller already holds
from the SpotGrid bot-info HTTP fetch (`SpotGridBotInfo.lastPrice`). A
blank seed is a no-op (the WS still fills it live). The `tickers` WS
continues to OVERRIDE this seed on every push, so the live ratio tracks
the freshest price exactly like the legacy `updateBenefitRatio`.

`paramsFromSelf` reflection emits whether or not anyone assigned it, because
a primitive has no "unset" state. Hence its position: last, outside the
assignment-ordered block above.

convention. `reduceOnly` / `major` / `associate` are strings *only* because

construction site rather than threaded through state: the arbitrage
place-order flow never writes the property (zero assignments under

checkbox this page has no counterpart to). Kept as a field anyway so a
future borrow rollout has the seam — but do not wire it to anything without
a native assignment to mirror.

name: signal_bot_max_drawdown_display_android
doc:
Android's MAX-DRAWDOWN formatter. Narrowed from an "indicator" catch-all:
the win-rate row does NOT need this — iOS's
`[[num treatAsPercentage] toLocalizedStringDownToFixed:2]`
(`OKTSSignalBotDetailViewModel.m:139`) and Android's
`formatICUPercent(DOWN, minMaxPrecision(2, 2), AUTO, x100)` are equivalent, and
a win rate is non-negative so the renderer's FLOOR equals DOWN. Win rate
therefore shares [`signal_bot_win_rate_display`] with iOS.

Max drawdown genuinely differs and cannot share
[`signal_bot_max_drawdown_display`]:

* iOS clamps a positive ratio below `0.001` UP to `0.001`
(`OKTStgyMaxDrawdownUtil.percentFixedNumberFromPlainString`) — "any drawdown
shows at least 0.10%". Android has no such rule; it reuses its win-rate
formatter (`BenefitDetailDataMapper.kt:1204`). **Whether Android is simply
missing this product rule is an open question for product/iOS.**
* A drawdown can be NEGATIVE (iOS branches on `isLessThanZero`), and there the
renderer's fixed FLOOR diverges from Android's DOWN — hence the pre-scaling
below.

Android's contract, from `formatIndicatorPercent`
(`BenefitDetailDataMapper.kt:1204`):
`OKTNumberF.formatPercent(x, roundMode = DOWN)` resolves to
`formatICUPercent(DOWN, minMaxPrecision(2, 2), AUTO, scale = 100)`.

**Pre-scaled on purpose.** `BotDisplayTextRenderer` hard-codes
`RoundingMode.FLOOR` for `Percent`, which equals Java's `DOWN` only for
non-negative input — a negative drawdown would diverge on the last decimal
(`-12.345` -> `-12.34` toward zero, `-12.35` toward -inf). Rust therefore
applies the ×100 and the toward-zero rounding itself, leaving the renderer's
FLOOR a no-op.

Blank -> `Placeholder`: native returns null for a blank ratio and the row
renders `--`. Unparseable -> **ZERO**, deliberately NOT the `Raw`
pass-through its two siblings use, because native's `toBigSafeDecimal`
coerces garbage to zero and the row shows `0.00%`.

Do **not** use [`signal_bot_max_drawdown_display`] on Android. That one
models iOS's three-step chain — a 0.001 small-positive clamp plus a per-sign
4-decimal pre-round — neither of which Android performs. Android has exactly
one indicator formatter, so both rows share this function.

name: replace_with_ws_data
doc:
Replace with an authoritative open-order snapshot. Used by BOTH platforms.

Android `TradeStrategyOrderBillDetailsTask` first applies incremental
socket rows to its private list and then publishes that FULL list. A
second merge would retain rows Android already removed. Empty is
meaningful and clears the tab.

iOS needs exactly the same entry, which is why this is no longer gated to
`cfg(any(test, target_os = "android"))`: native's `processWSData:` has a
snapshot branch as well — `data.count == 0` clears the list and
`data.count > 1` is the "first / timed / full push" that calls
`updateItems:data` outright (`OKTSSignalBotSubOrderDataSource.m:73-82`).
Neither is expressible through the merge entry, which can only
replace-matching / append-new and therefore keeps rows the snapshot
dropped.

This does NOT make `update_with_ws_data` redundant: iOS still routes the
single-row event pushes through it (insert / remove / coalesced update),
exactly as native does.

uniformly ms; nothing here is asymmetric.

so the crate held both spellings for one field while `cTime`/`uTime` in
the very same fixture were 13-digit ms. Both fixtures are ms now.
Nothing in the Rust twin depended on it — `resolve_next_purchase_visible`
(`displays.rs:410-416`) only probes parseability — which is why the
disagreement survived a green suite.

convertor and the quote convertor resolve through different instrument
fields and CAN differ (e.g. a `BTC-USD` instrument displayed as
`BTC-USDS` with `tradeQuoteCcy: USDC`). Native reads two different
convertors for these two rows; collapsing them into one field would be a
silent parity change.

(`param.quoteConvertor?.targetUnitPrecision ?? 2`). Without this field the
Rust arm would have to keep a convertor alive purely to recompute a value
the twins already resolved — a **dual-computed read**, which the
migration's definition of done does not permit waiving (unlike the
object-shaped `model:` argument those same sheets take).

detail page's rendered amounts cannot disagree.

fields.name: total_pnl_display
fields.doc:
A4a — Overview "Total PnL" amount half of the composite. Native
`OKTStgyPnlDispalyUtil.localizedPnl(withPnl:precision:)`: sign-dependent
truncation **toward zero** at the profit precision
(`plainPnlWithPnl` — negative `toPlainStringUpToMax`, positive
`toPlainStringDownToMax`), then an idempotent
`toLocalizedStringRoundToMax`, with "+" prepended on positives.
≡ `RoundingMode::Down` + `BotSignType::ExceptZero`, coloured by the raw
PnL sign.

The **composite** string (`"<pnl> (<ratio>)"`, reversed under RTL) is
assembled on the Swift side — it is a layout-direction concern
(`rtl_localizedStringWithProfit` branches on
`UIApplication.isLayoutRTL`), and joining two ICU-rendered numbers in
Rust would deny native its per-number `formatICUNumber` grouping pass.

fields.name: pnl_ratio_display
fields.doc:
A4b — Overview "Total PnL" ratio half. Native
`localizedPnlRatio(withPnlRatio:precision: 2)`: truncate toward zero,
`treatAsPercentage` (×100), `prependPlusSign`, then
`toLocalizedStringDownToFixed:2` → **FLOOR, FIXED 2 dp (trailing zeros
KEPT), no clamp**.

⚠️ Deliberately built with `percent_display` (raw ratio, native applies
the ×100 + FLOOR at 2) and **not** with
`format_util::pnl_ratio_total_display`, which mirrors the Kotlin
`fmtPnlPercent` and applies a `MAX_PERCENT_VALUE` **clamp that iOS does
not have**. Reusing the Kotlin builder would diverge for tiny ratios.

fields.name: pnl_ratio_chart_color
fields.doc:
A17 — the Overview **chart header's** PnL-ratio colour direction.

A separate field from [`Self::pnl_ratio_display`]'s own colour because the
chart header applies a **different rule to the same raw ratio** — the
R-B20 shape again:

| | Overview cell (A4b) | Chart header (A17) |
|---|---|---|
| Native leaf | `localizedPnlRatio(…)` + `pnlColor` | `okts_isGreaterThanOrEqualToZero()` |
| Compare digit | 2 (truncate) | **4 (half-up)** |
| Zero | Neutral | **Up** (`>= 0` is Rise) |
| Blank / non-numeric | no colour | `contentPrimary` (a third colour) |

The compare digit differing from the *display* digit is the trap: a ratio
of `-0.00001` renders as `"0.00%"` but is still a Fall, and comparing at 2
would flip it to Rise.

`None` encodes native's `contentPrimary` early return — reached when
`localizedPnlRatio(…, precision: 2)` yields nothing renderable (blank or
non-numeric ratio). It is NOT "colour unknown": the Swift row must render
`contentPrimary` for `None`, not Rise. Native reference:
`RecurringBuyDetailsOverviewChartInfoViewState.swift:47-55`.

fields.doc:

the bot is paused **or** `nextInvestTime` is blank/non-numeric

The date render itself stays native (`NSDate.fromTimestamp(ts / 1000)

the pause-state comparison never needs an `OKTOrderStatusType` constant

The RUNNING/PENDING arm is a separate, larger port (6 distinct ordered
lists, 19 item objects) and is NOT covered here — see the slice manifest's
"Scoped follow-up: Overview field grid".

Legacy `OKTAMenuFilter.menuArbitrageMarginListItem` builds this menu from
EVERY group `getFutureGroups` returns — one item per group, carrying its
`ctType` + `ccyType` (`OKTASMenuItem.itemId` / `.itemCcy`). That includes the
`linear` and `inverse` buckets; an interim adapter hid them, which this
restores (gap-3). The interactor derives the list from the buckets actually
present in the fetched data for the tab, in the canonical 5-bucket order
(`linear` / `USDT` / `USD` / `inverse` / `USDC`), so the VM/VC can build the
filter menu without re-deriving bucket keys client-side.

`ccy_type` matches the value `set_ccy_type` expects (from
`arb_bucket_ccy_type`); `ct_type` is the paired contract class (from
`arb_bucket_ct_type`). The empty-string ("All") menu item is a Swift concern
and is NOT included here.
